report.summary: Cause: in `public/src/store.js`, `ship()` changed the order object in place and then called `set({ orders: state.orders })` with the same array. `set()` skips the update when every changed value is the same reference as before, so no subscriber was notified and the row never re-rendered. A reload showed "Shipped" because the server had already saved it. Fix: after the server confirms, `ship()` now builds a new orders array with a new object for the shipped order, so the view re-renders and the Mark shipped button disappears. The failure path is unchanged: the row keeps its status and "Could not update the order." is shown. I also added two tests in `test/store.test.js`, one for a successful ship that notifies subscribers and one for a failed update.
report.verification: `npm test` passes (6 of 6, including the 2 new tests). I also started the server, opened Orders in Playwright Chromium, chose Packed and clicked Mark shipped on ORD-1002. The row changed to "Shipped" without a reload and its button was gone. I stopped the server by its process id afterwards. I did not run Recovery Probe. The project has no `.recovery-probe/verify.json`, and I had already changed the code, so a before-change baseline wasn't possible. I did not run the registry's `orders-ship-updates-row` check or `compare_reports`, so there is no Recovery Probe verdict.
